text:
ashley: Hey team, heads up — saw a big memory spike in staging after the autoslab allocator merge (PR #4821). A few long-context requests OOMed. Canary is on 3 nodes, 2 of them hit OOMs within the hour. @sre-oncall :eyes:

zack: Yikes. Is this the allocator change that changed slab coalescing thresholds?

ashley: Yep. It adjusted the coalesce window to be more aggressive to reduce fragmentation for short seqs, but looks like longctx behaviour worsened. Logs: 
```
2026-03-18T08:12:42Z infer[pid=4421]: kv_cache: slab_alloc: requested 128MB, available 64MB -> OOM
2026-03-18T08:12:42Z kernel-router: fallback triggered, selected slow kernel
2026-03-18T08:12:42Z infer[pid=4421]: runtime: panic: out of memory
```

marco: perf-bot flagged a CI regression on the kernel-selection perf job this morning, perf delta ~+28% p90 for the longseq benchmark. That lines up.

perf-bot: CI perf regression detected in job longseq-kernel-suite. First failing commit: 7c9a2d3 (autoslab/coalesce: tweak window). Median p90 increase: 28.3%.

elaine: I ran a quick flamegraph on the canary. The hotspot is still the KV evict path — more time spent scanning slabs and rebuilding freelists. Looks like the aggressive coalesce makes fewer but much larger slab moves, which fragment the heap for long sequences.

zack: Can we bisect to confirm? Start from prior release that was OK (tag v2026.02.11) -> HEAD. I'll run git bisect on the infra repo now.

zack: (running) ```
git bisect start
git bisect good v2026.02.11
git bisect bad HEAD
# testing 7c9a2d3
```

zack: Confirmed — bisect points to 7c9a2d3 and sibling 7c9a2d3~1 (both part of the same autoslab series). Reverting the patch locally fixes the OOMs and restores p90 kernel selection latency.

ashley: Thanks. I'm going to pin the rollout and open a rollback PR to revert the autoslab change for now. We should also add a regression test: run longseq workload in CI after allocator changes.

marco: Agree. Also let's add a canary gate: when allocator/coalesce params change, run a short longseq memory sweep (10k tokens) to catch seq-length sensitivity.

elaine: Quick patch idea: add a seqlen-weighted coalesce heuristic so we don't merge slabs if active longctx reservations exist. That should reduce fragmentation for long prompts. I'll prototype.

ashley: For immediate mitigation, rollback PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4902 (revert autoslab coalesce). Marking rollout hold. @sre-oncall please hold Dedicated rollouts until PR merged.

sre-oncall: On it. Holding Dedicated and Hosted canaries. Notifying CS that a small regression may affect a subset of long-context customers, ETA for revert review ~30m.

ci-bot: perf-job longseq-kernel-suite has been re-run with reverted commit; p90 back to baseline.

zack: Post-mortem action items: 1) Add longseq memory CI gate for allocator changes. 2) Add canary metric: slab-move-rate and avg-slab-size. 3) Prototype seqlen-aware coalesce. 4) Tag the allocator PR with perf/ci checklist.

ashley: Filing a short incident note and tagging the allocator team. We'll follow up with a proper postmortem once rollback completes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
